title: A trivial Kan fibration has a section that is a homotopy inverse
statement: Let $p:X\to Y$ be a trivial Kan fibration of simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], let $\Delta[1]$ be the simplicial set of that node, $X\times\Delta[1]$ the termwise product, and for $e\in\{0,1\}$ let $i_e:X\to X\times\Delta[1]$ be $x\mapsto(x,c_e)$ with $c_e\in\Delta[1]_k$ the constant map $[k]\to[1]$ with value $e$. Then there are a morphism of simplicial sets $g:Y\to X$ with $p\circ g=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and a morphism of simplicial sets $h:X\times\Delta[1]\to X$ with $h\circ i_0=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $h\circ i_1=g\circ p$ (a homotopy from $\mathrm{id}_X$ to $g\circ p$); in particular $p$ is a homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Simplicial, Lemma 08NS (label lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy, lines 5641-5664), using Lemma 08NM (label lemma-trivial-kan, lines 5550-5585); homotopy as in Definition 019K (definition-homotopy)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to the degreewise injection $\varnothing\to Y$, with its unique map $\varnothing\to X$ and the identity map $Y\to Y$. The resulting lift $g:Y\to X$ satisfies $p\circ g=\mathrm{id}_Y$.

source.place: Simplicial, Lemma Tag 08NS (lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy), proof, first sentence, applying Lemma Tag 08NM (lemma-trivial-kan)

proof.text: The inclusion $j:\partial\Delta[1]\times X\to\Delta[1]\times X$ is degreewise injective. Indeed, $\partial\Delta[1]$ consists in each degree of the two constant simplices $c_0,c_1$, so its product with $X$ is the disjoint union of two copies of $X$ and $j$ identifies them with the two endpoint subsets of $\Delta[1]\times X$. Define $a:\partial\Delta[1]\times X\to X$ to be $\mathrm{id}_X$ on the $c_0$ copy and $g\circ p$ on the $c_1$ copy, and $b:\Delta[1]\times X\to Y$ by $b=p\circ\mathrm{pr}_X$. On the first endpoint $p\circ a=p$; on the second $p\circ a=p\circ g\circ p=p$ by step 1. Hence $p\circ a=b\circ j$.

source.place: Simplicial, Lemma Tag 08NS (lemma-trivial-kan-homotopy), proof, displayed square and paragraph describing its maps

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to the commutative square of step 2. It gives $h:\Delta[1]\times X\to X$ with $h\circ j=a$ and $p\circ h=b$. Restricting $h\circ j=a$ to the two endpoint copies of $X$ gives $h\circ i_0=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $h\circ i_1=g\circ p$. This is the homotopy $h$ from $\mathrm{id}_X$ to $g\circ p$ required by the statement. Together with the strict equality $p\circ g=\mathrm{id}_Y$ from step 1, $g$ is a homotopy inverse to $p$.
